note: Research batch 5 (pest depth) for ChatGPT to plug into data.js. Every PMID verified against the NCBI E-utilities API (titles and years match). Each study tagged with plant (oilIds), terpenes (compoundIds), uses (categories). Merge rule: skip any study whose pubmedId already exists in data.js.

studies.title: In vitro insecticidal and repellent activity of Cymbopogon essential oils and geraniol against cat flea.
studies.authors: de Oliveira Chaves JK, Campos DR, Santos Soares EFM, et al.
studies.finding: Geraniol showed the lowest LC50 values against cat flea eggs, pupae, adults, and whole life-cycle inhibition, while Cymbopogon martinii (palmarosa) oil was most potent against larvae and kept repellency at 90% or higher for 48 hours.
studies.limitations: In vitro filter-paper assays only; no animal or field data.

studies.title: Insecticidal and Repellent Activity of Essential Oils from Copaifera reticulata, Citrus paradisi, Lavandula hybrida and Salvia sclarea Against Immature and Adult Stages of Ctenocephalides felis felis.
studies.authors: Lima EAS, Campos DR, Soares EFMS, et al.
studies.finding: All four oils showed insecticidal and repellent activity against cat flea life stages in vitro, with beta-caryophyllene-rich copaiba oil showing the strongest residual efficacy.
studies.limitations: In vitro only; Lavandula hybrida (lavandin) mapped to lavender; no host-animal testing.

studies.title: Acaricidal activity of Melaleuca alternifolia (tea tree) oil: in vitro sensitivity of sarcoptes scabiei var hominis to terpinen-4-ol.
studies.authors: Walton SF, McKinnon M, Pizzutto S, et al.
studies.finding: Five percent tea tree oil and its component terpinen-4-ol were highly effective at reducing scabies mite survival times in vitro, comparable to 5% permethrin and ivermectin.
studies.limitations: In vitro continuous-exposure assay; mites from a single crusted-scabies patient.

studies.title: In vitro activity of ten essential oils against Sarcoptes scabiei.
studies.authors: Fang F, Candy K, Melloul E, et al.
studies.finding: In contact assays 1% clove oil killed all scabies mites within 20 minutes and palmarosa within 50 minutes; efficacy order was clove, palmarosa, geranium, tea tree, then lavender.
studies.limitations: Mites from experimentally infected pigs; in vitro only.

studies.title: Biotoxicity of essential oil of Eucalyptus citriodora Hook (Myrtaceae) to dust mites.
studies.authors: Cai H, Xie P, Zhang X, et al.
studies.finding: Eucalyptus citriodora oil showed strong contact-fumigant toxicity to both house dust mite species, with citronellal the most toxic constituent and 100% vapor-phase mortality.
studies.limitations: Laboratory bioassays at high applied doses; no bedroom-scale testing.

studies.title: Repellent effect of oregano essential oil and carvacrol analogs against imported fire ants.
studies.authors: George G, Shah FM, Ali A, et al.
studies.finding: Oregano oil strongly repelled red and hybrid imported fire ants, with carvacrol (minimum repellent dose 0.98 ug/g) identified as the primary active constituent.
studies.limitations: Laboratory repellency assays; no field colony-level data.

studies.title: Common Home Remedies Do Not Deter Argentine Ants, Linepithema humile (Hymenoptera: Formicidae), from a Preferred Harborage.
studies.authors: Holloway JB, Suiter DR, Davis JW, et al.
studies.finding: MIXED RESULT: tansy, cucumber, and soybean-extract home remedies failed to deter Argentine ants even at 4 to 10 times the recommended dose, while 1% peppermint oil was the most deterrent treatment and fresh rosemary and spearmint leaves also deterred harboring.
studies.limitations: Laboratory harborage assay; short 2 to 4 hour observation window.

studies.title: Comparative repellency of 38 essential oils against mosquito bites.
studies.authors: Trongtokit Y, Rongsriyam Y, Komalamisra N, et al.
studies.finding: Of 38 oils screened on human forearms, only undiluted citronella, patchouli, clove, and makaen oils gave 2 hours of complete repellency against Aedes aegypti, with clove lasting longest (2 to 4 hours) across three mosquito species; no oil at 10 to 50% lasted 2 hours.
studies.limitations: Small volunteer panel; laboratory forearm assay, not field conditions.

studies.title: Larvicidal activity of essential oil from Vitex negundo and Vitex trifolia on dengue vector mosquito Aedes aegypti.
studies.authors: Chandrasekaran T, Thyagarajan A, Santhakumari PG, et al.
studies.finding: Vitex trifolia and Vitex negundo oils killed Aedes aegypti and Culex quinquefasciatus larvae at 50 to 125 ppm, with LC50 values around 51 to 58 ppm for Ae. aegypti.
studies.limitations: Laboratory larval assays; no field or non-target testing.

studies.title: Efficacy of Active Ingredients From the EPA 25(B) List in Reducing Attraction of Aedes aegypti (Diptera: Culicidae) to Humans.
studies.authors: Mitra S, Rodriguez SD, Vulcan J, et al.
studies.finding: NULL RESULT: rosemary oil showed no significant repellency against Aedes aegypti in the study's attraction assay, unlike peppermint oil which strongly reduced attraction at the first time point.
studies.limitations: Single laboratory assay design; short observation window.

studies.title: Experimental use of two standard tick collection methods to evaluate the relative effectiveness of several plant-derived and synthetic repellents against Ixodes scapularis and Amblyomma americanum (Acari: Ixodidae).
studies.authors: Schulze TL, Jordan RA, Dolan MC
studies.finding: In field-plot tick drags, nootkatone and a permethrin standard each repelled 100% of Ixodes scapularis nymphs through 14 days, slightly outperforming carvacrol (90.7%) and a plant-oil product (97.7%).
studies.limitations: Field-plot evaluation, not a controlled lab assay; nootkatone tested as an isolated compound rather than as grapefruit oil.

studies.title: Lemongrass essential oil and DEET inhibit attractant detection in infected and non-infected Ixodes scapularis ticks.
studies.authors: Gaudet K, Anholeto LA, Hillier NK, et al.
studies.finding: Exposure to lemongrass oil, citral, or geraniol significantly impaired adult female Ixodes scapularis ticks' ability to detect and respond to host attractant, regardless of pathogen infection status.
studies.limitations: Electrophysiology and Y-tube lab assays; behavioral disruption rather than bite prevention was measured.

newOils.name: Palmarosa
newOils.description: Steam-distilled from tropical grass. Very high in geraniol; top performer against cat fleas and scabies mites in comparative screens.
newOils.safety: Generally well tolerated; patch test for sensitive skin.

newOils.name: Copaiba
newOils.description: Steam-distilled oleoresin. Exceptionally rich in beta-caryophyllene; strongest residual efficacy against cat fleas in comparative testing.
newOils.safety: Generally well tolerated; patch test for sensitive skin.

newOils.name: Grapefruit
newOils.description: Cold-pressed from peel. Limonene-dominant like other citrus; botanical source of nootkatone, the 14-day tick repellent.
newOils.safety: Phototoxic risk; avoid sun exposure after topical use.

newOils.name: Clary Sage
newOils.description: Steam-distilled from flowering tops. Linalyl acetate dominant; tested against cat flea life stages.
newOils.safety: Avoid with alcohol; generally well tolerated otherwise.

newOils.name: Geranium
newOils.description: Steam-distilled from leaves. Citronellol and geraniol rich; third most effective oil against scabies mites in a ten-oil screen.
newOils.safety: Generally well tolerated; patch test for sensitive skin.

newOils.name: Vitex
newOils.description: Steam-distilled from leaves. Larvicidal against Aedes aegypti and Culex mosquitoes at 50 to 125 ppm.
newOils.safety: For external use; limited safety data — dilute well.

newCompounds.name: Nootkatone
newCompounds.description: Grapefruit-derived sesquiterpenoid; repelled 100% of Ixodes scapularis nymphs through 14 days in field trials.

newCompounds.name: Citronellol
newCompounds.description: Rosy alcohol prominent in geranium and citronella; softer counterpart to citronellal.
